excitation_report: Full child-vs-parent ODE-system comparison on the n(t) trajectory. New mechanism = auger_reinjection*n^2*T_e/(T_impact+T_e) (impact-ionization reinjection). At sigma=0.01 its peak effect on n(t) is 0.1274 abs = 12.7*sigma (>=5*sigma), strongest at t~0.75, where n is still large and T_e has risen from Joule/recombination heating. All inherited terms (linear -n/tau_n loss, coupling_np*p source, drift_saturation drift-loss, phonon-bottleneck recombination, carrier_temp_coupling Arrhenius channel) were dominant contributors to the RHS (order ~0.1-2) at check_substitution and drive the leading relaxation, so they remain well above sigma. Boosting T_e (joule_heating=recomb_heating=1.0), lowering T_impact=0.5 and setting auger_reinjection=0.5 (both at physical edge of suggested ranges) was needed to lift the new term from 1.1*sigma to 12.7*sigma.

rationale: Typed ODE-system contract inherited verbatim: state_variables, state_rhs, initial_conditions and target RHS are taken exactly as given; I only chose the time window, fixed parameter values, noise and expectations. Time range [0,10] with 300 linear points spans the fast early transient (dynamics peak near t~0.75) through full relaxation over several unit relaxation times. Relaxation times set to 1.0 and couplings to O(0.5) give a well-conditioned, finite trajectory (verified via check_substitution). The evolution's new impact-ionization reinjection term depends on T_e, which starts at 0, so it is only excited once heating raises T_e; increasing joule/recomb heating to 1.0, setting auger_reinjection=0.5 and T_impact=0.5 (edges of the suggested physical ranges) makes it reach 12.7*sigma at sigma=0.01, comfortably visible above noise.

scenario_text: In a conducting solid, an initial nonuniform population of charge carriers is prepared and then allowed to redistribute under internal scattering and drift processes. The carrier density and the associated internal drift momentum relax back toward equilibrium as collisions dissipate the excess and coupling between the population imbalance and the collective momentum produces transient adjustment. We track how the excess carrier density and the mean drift momentum jointly evolve in time after the perturbation is removed. The interest is in the coupled relaxation dynamics governed by scattering within the electronic subsystem.
